- **Compiled:** July 2026
- **Method:** Web research (WebSearch + WebFetch + raw-HTML inspection of charlottelatin.org
 pages for image URLs, since the site is a Finalsite build that lazy-loads images via
 `data-image-sizes` attributes rather than plain `src`).
- **Primary domain:** charlottelatin.org
- **Corroborating domains:** blumenthalarts.org (Blumey Awards nominee/winner releases)
- **Compiled by:** Claude research pass for the parent-facing school-comparison app

### Confidence key

- **[VERIFIED]** — read directly in a page fetched during this pass; source URL given.
- **[SCHOOL-CLAIM]** — the school asserts it on its own marketing page; not independently
 corroborated (e.g. participation rates, "nationally recognized").
- **[NOT FOUND]** — searched for and could not confirm. Never guessed or filled in.

sections.text:
### Scale and participation

- Charlotte Latin serves **more than 1,500 students in transitional kindergarten through
 twelfth grade** — TK-12. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-facilities
- **Over 80% of students participate in the arts at Latin.** **[SCHOOL-CLAIM]** — stated on
 the arts landing page; no methodology published (does not say whether it counts required
 Lower/Middle School arts classes, which would inflate it).
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts
- The arts landing page frames the ladder as **Lower School = "foundational skills,"
 Middle School = "exploration of mediums," Upper School = "advanced performances and
 portfolio work."** **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts

### Lower School (TK-Grade 4/5)

- **Experiential approach to music and theater**; youngest students learn "rhythm, melody,
 expression, genre — through singing, dancing, and playing." Young actors "develop through
 imaginative storytelling." **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Signature Grandparents' Day program** is the named Lower School performance tradition.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Guest artist presentations on campus reinforce classroom concepts** — this is the
 visiting-artist enrichment thread, though no individual visiting artists are named.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Band and stringed instruments are introduced in Grade 5**, explicitly described as "a
 bridge to Middle and Upper School programs." **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Fourth and fifth grade students present an age-appropriate musical each year.**
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
 - 2026-27 LS musical: ***Madagascar Kids***, January 28-29. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar
- Lower School visual art: students "learn form, style and technique through instruction"
 with cultural and historical context; the visual arts program **begins in transitional
 kindergarten**. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual

### Middle School (Grades 5-8)

- **Band, orchestra, choir, and theater courses are the foundation of the Middle and Upper
 School program**, with "many opportunities for ensemble and solo performance."
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Theater is available Grades 7-12; the backstage/technical course runs Grades 6-12** —
 note the tech course starts *earlier* than the acting course. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Grade 8 visual art is a self-designed course:** eighth graders "independently design
 their course in the visual arts and are free to sculpt, paint, draw, design, or photograph
 any subject area and in any genre they find interesting." This is the most distinctive
 single feature of Latin's visual-arts ladder — an independent-study structure two years
 before Upper School. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual
- Middle School students choose visual arts **electives**. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual

### Upper School (Grades 9-12)

- Same core ensemble offerings as Middle School (band, orchestra, choir, theater, backstage).
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Seniors may participate in a capstone film project.** **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- Visual art remains "hugely popular" as an Upper School elective. **[SCHOOL-CLAIM]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual
- **Typical Upper School load is five academic courses plus one enrichment class** — arts
 courses serve as that enrichment slot, which is the structural reason participation can run
 high. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings

### Upper School arts course list (from the Course Offerings page)

The following is the **complete** arts course list as published on Latin's Upper School
Course Offerings page. **[VERIFIED]**
https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings

**Visual Arts**
- Art Studio I
- Art Studio II
- Art Studio III
- Art Studio IV
- Photography

**Music**
- Band
- Concert Choir
- Orchestra
- Music Theory I
- **Music Theory AP**

**Drama / Theatre**
- Acting
- Film Acting
- Stagecraft I and II
- Advanced Design
- After-School Theater and Stagecraft

**Important reading of this list — the AP question.** The only AP arts course Latin publishes
is **AP Music Theory**. There is **no AP Studio Art / AP 2-D or 3-D Art & Design, no AP Art
History, and no separately named honors portfolio course** on the Course Offerings page.
**[VERIFIED — by absence]** The top of the visual-arts ladder is instead the numbered
sequence **Art Studio I → II → III → IV**, plus Photography. Anyone comparing Latin to peers
on "does it offer AP Studio Art" should treat this as a real structural difference, not a
publishing gap — the page does list AP for Music Theory, so the page does surface APs where
they exist.

- **[NOT FOUND]** A current downloadable Upper School course catalog PDF or Issuu edition
 with per-course *descriptions* (credit hours, prerequisites, portfolio requirements). The
 Course Offerings page carries names only, in a menu structure. An **Issuu edition exists
 but is stale — "Upper School Course Catalog 2020-21"**
 (https://issuu.com/charlottelatinschool/docs/uscoursecatalog_2020-21_web_feb20_20), five
 years out of date and not cited as current here. Latin publishes notably less course detail
 than several Charlotte peers.

### Ensembles (named)

- **Concert Choir (Grades 5-12)** — the one ensemble Latin names with an explicit grade span.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Band (Grades 6-12)** and **Orchestra (Grades 6-12)** — grade spans inferred from the
 concert titles on the arts calendar ("Grades 6-12 Band Concert," "Grades 6-12 Orchestra
 Concert," "Grades 6-12 Choir Concert"). **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar
- **Community Chorale** — a distinct ensemble with its own December concert date.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar
- **US Orchestra** and **MS Orchestra** perform separate spring concerts, so the strings
 program splits by division at the top end. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar
- **[NOT FOUND]** Named auditioned sub-ensembles — no jazz band, no a cappella group, no
 chamber orchestra, no show choir, no wind ensemble/symphonic band tiering is published
 anywhere on the arts pages. Latin's public ensemble picture is one band, one orchestra, one
 choir per division plus a Community Chorale.

### Facilities

- **Horne Performing Arts Center** — described by the school as **"the creative heartbeat of
 campus,"** a space where students "sing, act, move, and imagine together."
 **[SCHOOL-CLAIM / VERIFIED as the school's language]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts
- **Thies Auditorium** and **Anne's Black Box Theater** are named as spaces within the Horne
 Performing Arts Center. **[PARTIAL — treat with caution]** These names came from a Google
 search-result snippet attributed to a facilities page at
 `https://www.charlottelatin.org/arts/facilities`, but **that URL returns HTTP 404** when
 fetched directly, and the live page at `/the-arts/arts-facilities` contains **no text at
 all** (photo gallery only). So the two room names could not be confirmed on any live page in
 this pass. Verify on a tour before printing them.
- **Six visual art studios.** **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual
- **Fab Lab** — referenced on the arts landing page in connection with student portfolio work.
 **[VERIFIED, thin]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts — see 1d below; Latin does not
 publish an arts-specific Fab Lab description.
- **Student Art Gallery** (online student exhibition) and **Arts Walk** (permanent campus
 collection) — both are standing sections of the arts site. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/student-art-gallery-clone /
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/artswalk
- **Latin has a dedicated box office** — `boxoffice@charlottelatin.org`, with waitlist
 handling for sold-out shows. A small but telling operational detail: the theatre program is
 run like a ticketed venue. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **[NOT FOUND]** Seat counts for Thies Auditorium or the Black Box; a named dance studio; a
 photography darkroom; a dedicated ceramics/kiln room. The Arts Facilities page
 (https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-facilities) is a **photo gallery with no
 descriptive body text at all** — its only prose is the school's generic boilerplate.

### Enrichment and season structure

- **Arts Walk: Create and Celebrate** — an annual community arts event (October 24 in 2026-27),
 distinct from the permanent Arts Walk collection. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar
- **Mosaic Night** (April 9), **Behind the Curtain Event** (February 25), **Youth Art Month
 Opening Reception** (March 4), **Senior Art Show** (February 4), **Music Recitals** (May 2),
 **community sing-along**, and a **student fashion show**. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar and
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
### Latin Arts Association (LAA) — the parent arts organization

This is a real, well-structured parent booster organization and one of Latin's stronger arts
assets. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/latinartsassociation

- **The LAA is a parent *and faculty* organization** dedicated to enhancing the student arts
 experience. Its stated scope: *"We support Creative Writing, Music (Band, Choir, Orchestra),
 Speech & Debate, Theater Arts, and Visual Arts."* Note that Latin folds **Creative Writing
 and Speech & Debate into "the arts"** — a broader definition than most peer schools use.
- **Five standing committees**, each with its own chair: **Friends of Creative Writing**,
 **Friends of Music**, **Friends of Speech and Debate**, **Friends of Theater**, and
 **Friends of Visual Arts**.
- **Parent volunteer roles are concrete**, not nominal: ushering and ticketing for
 performances, backstage assistance and **costume work**, serving as **debate tournament
 judges**, donating refreshments, and supporting the publication ***The Blue Review***.
- **The LAA organizes auditions** for the fall play and musical, keeps a regular meeting
 schedule, and runs arts celebrations and workshops through the year.
- **2024-25 executive board:** President **Jen Wouters**; Vice Presidents **Carolyn Stone**
 and **Abbe McCracken**; Treasurer **Maria Hurden**; Secretary **Ivy Babcock**; Special
 Events **Brittany DuBose**. Each division (Lower, Middle, Upper) has **three at-large
 representatives**.
 - Worth noting for the theatre story: **Abbe McCracken** (VP) shares a surname with
 **Kate McCracken**, Latin's 2022 Best Actress Blumey winner — likely a parent of the
 program's most decorated performer. **[VERIFIED names; relationship inferred, not stated]**
- Parents join by emailing individual committee chairs directly.
- **[NOT FOUND]** LAA budget, annual fundraising totals, or a current (2025-26 / 2026-27)
 board roster — the published board is 2024-25.

sections.text:
### Does Charlotte Latin have Blumey history? YES — and it is substantial but front-loaded.

This is the headline correction to the working assumption. Latin is **not** a Blumey
non-participant. It has competed since the very first year and has **won the single biggest
acting award in the program**. But its recognition is concentrated in the 2010s and early
2020s, and its **recent** record is thin.

**The ledger (all [VERIFIED] on blumenthalarts.org):**

| Year | Latin's show | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 (inaugural, 1st annual) | *Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat* | **Nominated: Wells Fargo Best Musical**; **Nominated: Best Actor — Will Branner as Joseph** |
| 2022 (9th annual) | *Bright Star* | **WON: Best Actress — Kate McCracken as "Alice Murphy"**; **WON: Best Featured Performer — Dominick Charles as "Daryl"** |
| 2025 | *The Drowsy Chaperone* | **Nominated: Best Student Stage Manager — Claire Addison** |
| 2026 (ceremony May 17, 2026, Belk Theater) | *Cabaret* | **Competed; received NO nominations in any category** |

Sources:
- Inaugural 2012 nominees (Best Musical + Will Branner, Best Actor):
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/blumenthal-performing-arts-announces-the-inaugural-blumey-awards-nominees
- 2022 winners (Kate McCracken, Best Actress; Dominick Charles, Best Featured Performer, both
 in *Bright Star*):
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/blumenthal-performing-arts-announced-the-9th-annual-blumey-awards-winners
- 2025 nominees (Claire Addison, Best Student Stage Manager, *The Drowsy Chaperone*):
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/2025-blumey-awards-nominations
- 2026 final nominees — Latin listed among the **59 competing schools** with *Cabaret*, with
 **no nomination in any category**:
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/2026blumeyawardsnominees

**Honest read for the card.** A **Best Actress Blumey (2022) is a top-line credential** — it
is the marquee individual award in the region's high-school musical theatre program, and Latin
also took Best Featured Performer the same night for the same show. That is a genuine peak.
But the trajectory since is modest: one stage-manager nomination in 2025 (a craft category,
not performance) and **zero nominations in 2026** despite mounting *Cabaret*. Latin competes
every year against a 59-school field; it is a real participant, not a dominant one. If the
card shows a ledger, showing all four years including the 2026 shutout is the accurate
presentation — cherry-picking 2022 would overstate the program's current standing.

### Productions — current and recent titles

**2026-27 season [VERIFIED]** — https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar

- **US Fall Play: *The Trial*** — October 9-11, 2026. (A Kafka adaptation; a notably
 un-crowd-pleasing, literary choice for a fall play.)
- **MS Musical: *Into the Woods, Jr.*** — November 13-14, 2026
- **LS Musical: *Madagascar Kids*** — January 28-29, 2027
- **US Musical: *The Little Mermaid*** — February 26-28, 2027 (this will be Latin's 2027
 Blumey entry)
- **MS Play: *The Odyssey*** — May 7-8, 2027

**2025-26 season [VERIFIED, partial]**

- **US Musical: *Cabaret*** — confirmed two independent ways: Latin's performing arts page
 notes a recent production of *Cabaret* that **SOLD OUT** (with box-office waitlist), and
 the 2026 Blumey release lists Charlotte Latin School / *Cabaret* among competing schools.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing and
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/2026blumeyawardsnominees
- **[NOT FOUND]** The 2025-26 **fall play** title. The arts calendar has already rolled over
 to 2026-27 and the prior season's titles are no longer posted. Auditions events ("US Fall
 Play Auditions," "MS Musical Auditions") appear on the calendar without titles attached.
- **2025 US Musical: *The Drowsy Chaperone*** (2024-25 season) — **[VERIFIED]** via the 2025
 Blumey nominees release.
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/2025-blumey-awards-nominations

### Theatre staff and tech

- **Alicia Long — Head of Performing Arts Program / Chair of Performing Arts.** **[VERIFIED]**
 Title appears as "Chair of Performing Arts" on the arts landing page and "Head of Performing
 Arts Program" on the performing arts page. https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts and
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **[NOT FOUND]** A named **theatre director** and a named **technical director**. Latin does
 not publish individual performing-arts faculty names on its arts pages beyond Alicia Long
 (and Pam Sweer, Assistant Band Director, who surfaced only via a news post). This is a real
 transparency gap versus peers who list a full arts faculty roster.
- **Tech-theatre course path [VERIFIED]:** **Stagecraft I and II** and **Advanced Design** in
 the Upper School catalog, plus **After-School Theater and Stagecraft**, and the
 **backstage technical course spanning Grades 6-12**. The tech track is genuinely
 articulated — it starts in Grade 6, has two sequenced Stagecraft courses and a capstone-ish
 Advanced Design, and produced a Blumey stage-manager nomination in 2025. For a family whose
 student is a techie rather than a performer, this is one of Latin's stronger arts stories.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings

### NCTC (North Carolina Theatre Conference)

- **[NOT FOUND]** Any Charlotte Latin NCTC high-school play festival results, regional
 placements, or advancement to state. No mention on Latin's site and nothing surfaced in
 search. Latin's competitive theatre identity is Blumey-based (musical), not NCTC-based
 (play festival).

sections.text:
### Ensembles by type

**Curricular (open-enrollment, credit-bearing) [VERIFIED]** —
https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings and
https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing

- **Band** (Grades 6-12)
- **Orchestra** (Grades 6-12; splits into MS Orchestra and US Orchestra for spring concerts)
- **Concert Choir** (Grades 5-12)

**Auditioned**

- **[NOT FOUND]** Latin publishes **no auditioned sub-ensembles** — no jazz ensemble, no
 a cappella, no chamber group, no honors/select choir. This is worth stating plainly: unlike
 peers that tier band into concert/symphonic/wind ensemble by audition, Latin's public music
 structure appears to be single-track per division. There is "a place for both the most
 advanced student and those trying something new for the first time" — the school's own
 framing suggests deliberate inclusivity over tiering. **[SCHOOL-CLAIM]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Community Chorale** — exists as a separate ensemble with its own concert; whether it is
 auditioned or open (or includes adults/parents) is **[NOT FOUND]**.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar

**Classroom / theory**

- **Music Theory I** and **Music Theory AP** — a genuine two-step theory path culminating in
 an AP exam. This is Latin's only arts AP. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings

### Staff

- **Alicia Long — Head of Performing Arts Program / Chair of Performing Arts.** **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **Pam Sweer — Assistant Band Director.** **[VERIFIED]** Quoted in the All-State news post:
 "Students chosen for All-State Honors Band serve as ambassadors for their school, showcasing
 the success that comes through hard work and perseverance."
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/school-news/news-details/~board/kudos/post/latin-eighth-grader-earns-seat-in-all-state-honors-band
- **[NOT FOUND]** Names for **Director of Bands**, orchestra director, and choral director.
 Only an *Assistant* Band Director is publicly named, which is an odd gap.

### External honors

**All-State Honors Band — 2026 [VERIFIED, with full detail]**

- **Sofia Rodrigues Angrisano**, **eighth grade**, **clarinet**.
- Auditioned successfully for the **South Central District Band Association** honor band and
 earned a seat in the **All-State Honors Band**, recognized by the **NC Music Educators
 Association**.
- Audition held at the **UNC Greensboro** campus; she placed **11th chair out of 20 available
 spots** in the ensemble.
- Announced **May 9, 2026**.
- Source:
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/about/school-news/news-details/~board/kudos/post/latin-eighth-grader-earns-seat-in-all-state-honors-band
- **Why this matters for a parent:** an *eighth grader* earning an All-State Honors Band chair
 is a strong signal — she cleared a statewide audition while still in Middle School. Also
 note the framing: the school ran this as a standalone "Kudos" news post, which suggests it
 is an uncommon achievement at Latin rather than an annual routine.

**Other music honors**

- **[NOT FOUND]** All-State **Chorus** selections. **[NOT FOUND]** All-State **Orchestra**
 selections. **[NOT FOUND]** Any additional All-State Band students in other years — the
 2026 post names no one else and says "Other Students Named: None."
- **[NOT FOUND]** **NCAIS** (North Carolina Association of Independent Schools) honors
 band/chorus/orchestra participation or selections.
- **[NOT FOUND]** **Adjudicated festival ratings** (MPA / Music Performance Adjudication
 Superior ratings, festival scores) — Latin publishes none.
- **[NOT FOUND]** **Tri-M Music Honor Society** chapter at Charlotte Latin.

Taken together: Latin's publicly documented music-honors record is **one named All-State
student (2026)**. That is a thin external-validation trail for a 1,500-student school, and
the card should not imply more.

sections.text:
### Media and studios

- **Six studios.** **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual
- Media named in the eighth-grade self-designed course description: **sculpt, paint, draw,
 design, or photograph** — i.e. sculpture, painting, drawing, design, photography.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual
- **Fashion / fiber work is clearly practiced** even though it is not a named course — see the
 Scholastic recognitions below (two separate fashion pieces) and the **student fashion show**
 listed as a department-supported community project. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/performing
- **[NOT FOUND]** Per-studio media assignments (which of the six studios is ceramics vs.
 darkroom vs. digital); kiln, printmaking press, or darkroom specifics.

### Course path to the top

- **Art Studio I → Art Studio II → Art Studio III → Art Studio IV**, plus **Photography**.
 **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/academics/upper-school/course-offerings
- **Confirmed from the catalog page: there is NO AP Studio Art (AP 2-D/3-D Art & Design or AP
 Drawing), NO AP Art History, and no separately named Honors Portfolio course.**
 **[VERIFIED — by absence, on a page that does list Music Theory AP]** The capstone is
 **Art Studio IV** plus the **Senior Art Show** (February 4 on the 2026-27 calendar), not an
 AP portfolio submission.
- The earlier **Grade 8 self-designed course** is effectively an independent-study on-ramp
 into that sequence. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual

### Faculty

- **Richard Fletcher — Chair of Visual Arts.** **[VERIFIED]** Named on the arts landing page,
 and independently corroborated by an image asset on that page filed as
 `RichardFletcherinUSclass.jpg` — i.e. Fletcher teaching an Upper School class.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts
- **[NOT FOUND]** Any other visual-arts faculty names. The visual arts page names **no
 faculty at all**; it refers only to "a team of dedicated and experienced art educators."

### Exhibition calendar

Latin runs a real, multi-event exhibition year — this is one of the program's genuine
strengths. **[VERIFIED]** https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar

- **Senior Art Show** — February 4
- **Youth Art Month Opening Reception** — March 4
- **Arts Walk: Create and Celebrate** — October 24 (community-facing arts event)
- **Mosaic Night** — April 9
- **Student Art Gallery** — a standing **online** exhibition organized by division (Lower,
 Middle, Upper School), framed as "a learning tool where student exhibitions function as
 development opportunities for personal artistic voice," emphasizing artistic process and
 historical context over isolated activities. **[VERIFIED]**
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/student-art-gallery-clone
 - Student artists listed there include **Hope Gottschling** (Upper School),
 **Madison Nabors** (Upper School, multiple entries), **Sloan Ellison** (Upper School,
 multiple entries), **Marion DuBose** (Upper School, multiple entries), and
 **Ellen Chapman** (Middle School, multiple entries). **[VERIFIED]**
- **Arts Walk — permanent campus art collection.** **[VERIFIED]** The Arts Walk page carries a
 substantial photographed collection of named works installed around campus. Titles readable
 from the page's own image assets include **Wingspan**, **The Hawk**, **The Finish Line**,
 **The Hurdler**, **Lucky 8**, **"Eyes Up" Reflection Garden Mosaic**, **Torsionsphere**,
 **Girl on Swing**, **Back to Back**, **Crater**, **Etched Glass Murals**, and the
 **Nurkin Hawk**. https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/artswalk
 - Note: several of these are athletics-themed (*The Hurdler*, *The Finish Line*,
 *Wingspan*, *The Hawk*), so the permanent collection reads partly as school-identity
 sculpture rather than a purely fine-art collection. **[VERIFIED — from asset titles]**

### Scholastic Art & Writing Awards

Latin does have a documented Scholastic trail, and it is **stronger than "one honorable
mention"** — the visual arts page hosts a set of images filed under a `/Scholastic/` asset
path, which is how the school archives its Scholastic-recognized work. **[VERIFIED]**
https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual

- **Hope Gottschling '24 — fashion work.** **[VERIFIED]** The arts landing page hosts her
 piece as `24_Gottschling_Hope_SilkStrength_FashionLarge.jpg` — filed as class of **'24**,

### The Fab Lab's cross-disciplinary role

sections.text:
### Reasons the arts program holds up (concrete)

1. **A real Blumey win at the top of the region's marquee category.** Kate McCracken took
 **Best Actress at the 2022 Blumeys** for *Bright Star*, and Dominick Charles took **Best
 Featured Performer** the same night. In a 59-school regional field, a Best Actress win is
 the single most competitive individual honor available, and Latin has one.
 https://www.blumenthalarts.org/news/detail/blumenthal-performing-arts-announced-the-9th-annual-blumey-awards-winners

2. **A genuinely articulated technical-theatre track — rare and undersold.** Backstage tech
 starts in **Grade 6** (a year *before* the acting course), and the Upper School sequence
 runs **Stagecraft I → Stagecraft II → Advanced Design**, plus an after-school stagecraft
 option. It produced a **2025 Blumey nomination for Best Student Stage Manager (Claire
 Addison, *The Drowsy Chaperone*)**. For a student who wants to build rather than perform,
 this is a stronger offering than most peer schools publish.

3. **An unusual independent-study on-ramp in visual art at Grade 8.** Eighth graders
 "independently design their course in the visual arts" — free to sculpt, paint, draw,
 design, or photograph any subject in any genre. Self-directed portfolio behavior two years
 before Upper School is a structural advantage, not a marketing line.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/visual

4. **A dense, year-round exhibition and performance calendar with named events, not vague
 promises.** Five theatrical productions across three divisions in 2026-27 (*The Trial*,
 *Into the Woods Jr.*, *Madagascar Kids*, *The Little Mermaid*, *The Odyssey*), six-plus
 concerts, **Senior Art Show**, **Youth Art Month reception**, **Mosaic Night**, **Arts
 Walk: Create and Celebrate**, and **Music Recitals**. The Upper School fall play is
 *The Trial* — a Kafka adaptation, which signals a program willing to program literary
 material rather than only crowd-pleasers.
 https://www.charlottelatin.org/the-arts/arts-calendar

5. **Documented Scholastic Art & Writing recognition including a Gold Key** (Ella Hennessy
 '28, "Strike," Photography), spanning multiple media and multiple years — fashion, oil
 painting, drawing, photography. Plus **an eighth grader earning an All-State Honors Band
 chair (Sofia Rodrigues Angrisano, clarinet, 11th of 20, 2026)** — statewide validation
 achieved while still in Middle School.

6. **Sold-out demand and box-office infrastructure.** *Cabaret* sold out with a managed
 waitlist through a dedicated `boxoffice@charlottelatin.org`. The program operates as a
 ticketed venue, which implies real community draw.

### Where a parent should press — sharp tour questions

1. **"You offer AP Music Theory but no AP Studio Art, AP 2-D/3-D Art & Design, or AP Art
 History. If my child wants to submit a college-level studio portfolio, what is the path
 past Art Studio IV — and how do your seniors' portfolios compete without an AP framework?"**
 (This is the biggest documented structural gap; the catalog lists AP where it exists, so
 the absence is real.)

2. **"Latin had two Blumey wins in 2022, one stage-manager nomination in 2025, and zero
 nominations for *Cabaret* in 2026. What changed, and what does the trajectory of the
 musical theatre program look like going into *The Little Mermaid*?"**

3. **"Your public materials name Alicia Long, Richard Fletcher, and an assistant band
 director — but no Director of Bands, no orchestra director, no choral director, and no
 theatre or technical director. Who actually leads each ensemble and the theatre, and how
 long have they been here?"** (Turnover and thin naming often travel together.)

4. **"There's one band, one orchestra, and one choir per division with no auditioned or
 tiered ensembles published — no jazz band, no a cappella, no chamber or wind ensemble. How
 does an advanced player who's already at All-State level keep progressing here rather than
 coasting?"** (Sofia's case makes this concrete.)

5. **"How is the Fab Lab actually used by the arts department, as opposed to Innovation &
 Design? Can you walk me through one project from the last year where a student combined
 digital fabrication with studio art?"**

6. **"You cite over 80% arts participation. Does that count required Lower and Middle School
 arts classes, or only elective/ensemble enrollment in the Upper School — and what is the
 Upper School–only number?"**

7. **"Six studios — which media does each one hold? Is there a kiln, a darkroom, a
 printmaking press, and a dedicated dance studio?"** (The Arts Facilities page is photos
 only, with zero descriptive text.)

---

The Arts at Charlotte Latin School
Charlotte Latin School (TK-12, non-sectarian) - Charlotte, NC - Parent-Facing Deep
Research Report
Compiled research note - Charlotte private school arts programs. Prepared July 2026. Draft for family review.
Executive Summary
Charlotte Latin offers a broad, well-resourced, and highly participatory arts program: more than 80% of
its 1,500+ students take part. Anchored by the Horne Performing Arts Center and enriched by a Fab
Lab, a Student Art Gallery, and a campus-wide Arts Walk, the program pairs strong facilities with
practicing-artist faculty. Visual arts students reach the national stage through Scholastic Art & Writing
recognition, and musicians earn All-State Honors selections. Latin's distinctive edge is the integration
of art, design, and technology (the Fab Lab) within a mainstream, everyone-welcome arts culture.
Strengths
• Exceptional participation rate (80%+) - arts are central, not peripheral.
• Strong dedicated facilities (Horne PAC, studios, gallery) plus a Fab Lab for cross-disciplinary making.
• National/regional visual arts recognition and honors-ensemble music pipeline.
• Practicing-artist faculty leadership (Alicia Long, performing arts; Richard Fletcher, visual arts).
• Public-facing culture: Arts Walk, Student Art Gallery, and a full community-oriented arts calendar.
Questions for a Visit
• What advanced/honors and portfolio tracks exist in visual and performing arts?
• How do students access the Fab Lab for arts projects, and what has it produced?
• What are the audition norms for select ensembles and lead roles?
• How many students pursue the arts at the college level, and where?
• What does the 2025-26 production and concert season include?
Caveats
Synthesized from Charlotte Latin's public arts pages and recent school news (2025-26). Some
per-discipline course specifics are summarized at the program level where detailed lists were not
published online; confirm current details with the school (see Sources).

Charlotte Latin School (TK-12, non-sectarian) - Charlotte, NC - Arts Facilities

Horne Performing Arts Center
The Horne Performing Arts Center is described as the "creative heartbeat of campus" - the primary
venue for concerts, theatrical productions, and community arts events, supporting vocal, instrumental,
theatrical, and movement work.
Studios, Gallery & Fab Lab
• Visual arts studios distributed across the Lower, Middle, and Upper Schools.
• A dedicated Student Art Gallery for rotating exhibitions.
• A Fab Lab supporting design and fabrication that arts students use for cross-disciplinary projects.
Arts Walk
Beyond dedicated rooms, Latin curates "Arts Walk," a permanent collection of art installed throughout
the campus, so that visual art is part of the everyday environment.
Note
For room-by-room detail and capacities, see the school's Arts Facilities page (linked in Sources);
specifics are best confirmed on a campus visit.

The Arts at Charlotte Latin School
Charlotte Latin School (TK-12, non-sectarian) - Charlotte, NC - Program Overview
Compiled research note - Charlotte private school arts programs. Prepared July 2026. Draft for family review.
At a Glance
Charlotte Latin - a non-sectarian, coeducational, college-prep day school serving 1,500+ students
TK-12 - treats the arts as "integral to our learning and life experiences." Over 80% of students
participate in the arts. The multidisciplinary program is organized into Visual Arts and Performing
Arts, progressing from foundational skills in Lower School to advanced performances and portfolio
work in Upper School.
What Stands Out
• 80%+ participation - arts are a mainstream part of the Latin experience, not a niche.
• The Horne Performing Arts Center, described as the "creative heartbeat" of campus.
• A Fab Lab that arts students use for cross-disciplinary work (e.g., a student-designed, sewn, and
photographed fashion portfolio).
• Arts Walk - a permanent collection of art installed across campus.
• A dedicated Student Art Gallery and a full Arts Calendar of concerts, productions, and special
events.
• Regional and national student recognition, including the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards and
All-State Honors ensembles.
Leadership
The program is led by faculty who are practicing artists, including Alicia Long (chair of performing arts)
and Richard Fletcher (chair of visual arts), fostering what the school describes as a dynamic, inclusive
environment where bold expression is celebrated.
Journey Across Divisions
Lower School builds foundational technique; Middle School emphasizes exploration of mediums and
self-directed projects; Upper School moves to advanced performance and portfolio development - a
continuous creative arc TK-12.

Charlotte Latin - Visual Arts
Charlotte Latin School (TK-12, non-sectarian) - Charlotte, NC - Visual Arts
Compiled research note - Charlotte private school arts programs. Prepared July 2026. Draft for family review.
Program
"Visual art is everywhere" at Latin - lining hallways and filling studios. Students move from foundational
techniques in Lower School to self-directed projects in Middle and Upper School, encouraged to
"explore without limits" under the guidance of practicing-artist faculty (chaired by Richard Fletcher).
Cross-Disciplinary Making (Fab Lab)
Latin's Fab Lab extends visual arts into design and fabrication. A notable example: Hope Gottschling
'24 designed, sewed, and photographed a portfolio of fashion pieces that earned an honorable mention
in the National Scholastic Art & Writing Awards - illustrating how studio art, design, and technology
intersect at Latin.
Exhibition & Recognition
• A dedicated Student Art Gallery for exhibiting student work.
• Arts Walk - a permanent collection of art across campus.
• Student work "often earns regional and national recognition," including Scholastic Art & Writing
Awards (which the school has celebrated across 100 years of the program).
